motion.duration.100.$description: Default duration. Pick the step that matches the size and emphasis of the motion.

motion.easing.ease-in.$description: Ease-in curve. Use for elements leaving the viewport — slow start, accelerating exit.

motion.easing.ease-in-out.$description: Ease-in-out curve. Use for movements that both originate and settle on screen (e.g. expansions in place).

motion.easing.ease-out.$description: Ease-out curve. Use for elements entering the viewport — fast start, gentle settle.

motion.easing.emphasized.$description: Emphasised easing curve. Use for transitions that should feel more expressive (e.g. brand-led page transitions, hero reveal motion).

layout.divider.brand.size.$description: Brand divider size. The length of a brand-marked divider element.

layout.divider.brand.thickness.$description: Brand divider thickness. The cross-axis dimension of a brand-marked divider.

radius.ratio.default.$description: Default radius ratio. Multiplier for computing radius from a known element dimension (e.g. shortest side × ratio).

radius.ratio.lg.$description: Large radius ratio. For more pronounced proportional rounding.

radius.2xs.$description: Radius 2xs. Minimal rounding for very small elements (default focus rings, small boxes).

radius.xs.$description: Radius xs. Small rounding for compact UI elements (menu items, code spans), or for elements where relative size shouldn't be assumed (images).

radius.sm.$description: Radius sm. Moderate rounding for medium-scale UI surfaces.

radius.md.$description: Radius md. Default rounding for standard UI surfaces (alerts, code blocks). Pick t-shirt sizes when the element's shortest side is unknown — match the size to the component's relative scale.

radius.lg.$description: Radius lg. Pronounced rounding for large surfaces (cards, panels).

shape.logo.primary.view-box.$description: SVG viewBox dimensions for the primary logo.

shape.logo.primary.path.$description: SVG path data for the primary logo.

shape.logo.secondary.view-box.$description: SVG viewBox dimensions for the secondary logo lockup.

shape.logo.secondary.path.$description: SVG path data for the secondary logo lockup.

shape.logo.typographic.view-box.$description: SVG viewBox dimensions for the typographic logo (wordmark only).

shape.logo.typographic.path.$description: SVG path data for the typographic logo (wordmark only).

shape.logo.graphic.view-box.$description: SVG viewBox dimensions for the graphic logo (mark only).

shape.logo.graphic.path.$description: SVG path data for the graphic logo (mark only).

shape.tile.view-box.$description: SVG viewBox dimensions for the decorative tile.

shape.tile.path.$description: SVG path data for the decorative tile.

shape.tile-light.view-box.$description: SVG viewBox dimensions for the decorative light tile.

shape.tile-light.path.$description: SVG path data for the decorative light tile.

shape.tile-dark.view-box.$description: SVG viewBox dimensions for the decorative dark tile.

shape.tile-dark.path.$description: SVG path data for the decorative dark tile.

typography.font-family.default.$description: Default font family. Use as the system's standard typeface.

typography.font-stretch.normal.$description: Normal font width. Use as the system's standard type width.

typography.font-stretch.semi-condensed.$description: Semi-condensed font width. A subtly narrower alternative to normal.

typography.font-stretch.condensed.$description: Condensed font width. Use where horizontal space is tight (e.g. badges, avatars).

typography.font-stretch.ultra-condensed.$description: Ultra-condensed font width. The narrowest width; use sparingly for dense numeric/marker contexts.

typography.font-variation-settings.defau.$description: Default font-variation-settings. Restate after every `font` shorthand.

typography.font-variation-settings.itali.$description: Font-variation-settings for italic text. Adds the slant axis that WebKit drops when font-variation-settings is set — apply wherever `font-style: italic` is used.

typography.font-weight.regular.$description: Regular font weight. Use as the system's standard text weight.

typography.font-weight.regular-plus.$description: Slightly heavier regular font weight. Use for subtly emphasised text where bold would be too strong.

typography.font-weight.medium.$description: Medium font weight. Use for medium text emphasis (e.g. medium headings).

typography.font-weight.bold.$description: Bold font weight. Use for strong text emphasis (semantic `strong`/`b` elements, small headings).

typography.prose-link.default.decoration.$description: Default decoration line for prose links.
Default decoration offset for prose links, in em.
Default decoration thickness for prose links.

typography.prose-link.hover.decoration.l.$description: Decoration line for prose links on hover.

typography.prose-link.hover.decoration.o.$description: Decoration offset for prose links on hover, in em.

typography.prose-link.active.decoration..$description: Decoration offset for prose links during active (pressed) state, in em.

typography.text.body.xs.font.$description: Extra small body text. Use for the smallest body copy (microtext).

typography.text.body.xs.font-stretch.$description: Font width paired with the body xs composite.

typography.text.body.sm.font.$description: Small body text. Use for secondary copy (labels, captions, helper text) where default body would be too prominent.

typography.text.body.sm.font-stretch.$description: Font width paired with the body sm composite.

typography.text.body.md.font-stretch.$description: Font width paired with the body md composite.

typography.text.body.lg.font.$description: Large body text. Use for emphasised copy (intro paragraphs, lede text).

typography.text.body.lg.font-stretch.$description: Font width paired with the body lg composite.

typography.text.body.responsive.xs.font.$description: Extra small body text. Use for the smallest body copy (microtext).

typography.text.body.responsive.xs.font-.$description: Font width paired with the body responsive xs composite.

typography.text.body.responsive.sm.font.$description: Small body text. Use for secondary copy (labels, captions, helper text) where default body would be too prominent.

typography.text.body.responsive.sm.font-.$description: Font width paired with the body responsive sm composite.

typography.text.body.responsive.md.font-.$description: Font width paired with the body responsive md composite.

typography.text.body.responsive.lg.font.$description: Large body text. Use for emphasised copy (intro paragraphs, lede text).

typography.text.body.responsive.lg.font-.$description: Font width paired with the body responsive lg composite.

typography.text.heading.xs.font.$description: Extra small heading (`h6`-equivalent). Use for subsection headings.

typography.text.heading.xs.font-stretch.$description: Font width paired with the heading xs composite.

typography.text.heading.sm.font.$description: Small heading (`h5`-equivalent). Use for subsection headings.

typography.text.heading.sm.font-stretch.$description: Font width paired with the heading sm composite.

typography.text.heading.md.font.$description: Medium heading (`h4`-equivalent). Use for subsection headings.

typography.text.heading.md.font-stretch.$description: Font width paired with the heading md composite.

typography.text.heading.lg.font.$description: Large heading (`h3`-equivalent). Use for subsection headings and component-level titles (cards, panels).

typography.text.heading.lg.font-stretch.$description: Font width paired with the heading lg composite.

typography.text.heading.xl.font.$description: Extra large heading (`h2`-equivalent). Use for section headings.

typography.text.heading.xl.font-stretch.$description: Font width paired with the heading xl composite.

typography.text.heading.2xl.font-stretch.$description: Font width paired with the heading 2xl composite.

typography.text.heading.3xl.font.$description: Display heading (3xl). Use for hero/marketing headings.

typography.text.heading.3xl.font-stretch.$description: Font width paired with the heading 3xl composite.

typography.text.heading.4xl.font.$description: Display heading (4xl). Use for larger hero/marketing headings.

typography.text.heading.4xl.font-stretch.$description: Font width paired with the heading 4xl composite.

typography.text.heading.5xl.font.$description: Display heading (5xl). Use for the largest hero/marketing headings.

typography.text.heading.5xl.font-stretch.$description: Font width paired with the heading 5xl composite.

typography.text.heading.responsive.xs.fo.$description: Extra small heading (`h6`-equivalent). Use for subsection headings.
Font width paired with the heading responsive xs composite.

typography.text.heading.responsive.sm.fo.$description: Small heading (`h5`-equivalent). Use for subsection headings.
Font width paired with the heading responsive sm composite.

typography.text.heading.responsive.md.fo.$description: Medium heading (`h4`-equivalent). Use for subsection headings.
Font width paired with the heading responsive md composite.

typography.text.heading.responsive.lg.fo.$description: Large heading (`h3`-equivalent). Use for subsection headings and component-level titles (cards, panels).
Font width paired with the heading responsive lg composite.

typography.text.heading.responsive.xl.fo.$description: Extra large heading (`h2`-equivalent). Use for section headings.
Font width paired with the heading responsive xl composite.

typography.text.heading.responsive.2xl.f.$description: Font width paired with the heading responsive 2xl composite.

typography.text.heading.responsive.3xl.f.$description: Display heading (3xl). Use for hero/marketing headings.
Font width paired with the heading responsive 3xl composite.

typography.text.heading.responsive.4xl.f.$description: Display heading (4xl). Use for larger hero/marketing headings.
Font width paired with the heading responsive 4xl composite.

typography.text.heading.responsive.5xl.f.$description: Display heading (5xl). Use for the largest hero/marketing headings.
Font width paired with the heading responsive 5xl composite.

typography.word-spacing.default.$description: Default word spacing (in em). Tightens the space between words to suit the system's typeface.

typography.word-spacing.monospaced.$description: Word spacing for monospaced text (0em). Monospace glyphs carry their own even advance, so tightening word spacing would break the grid — apply to `code`, tabular data, and other mono contexts.

typography.leading.700.$description: Default leading dimension. A block size representing the line-height; apply it directly as a line-height value (a length is valid as-is — calc() cannot divide it by a font size cross-browser). An escape hatch for aligning line-heights across elements with different font sizes (e.g. a small counter beside a large heading) — reach for text composites or typeStep pairs first.

typography.paragraph.spacing.sm.$description: Tighter paragraph spacing. Use in dense layouts or compact prose.

typography.paragraph.spacing.lg.$description: Looser paragraph spacing. Use in editorial layouts where extra breathing room aids reading.

typography.metric.default.cell.height.$description: Character cell height (full line box), in em.

typography.metric.default.side-bearing.s.$description: A single per-side sidebearing, in em.

typography.metric.default.side-bearing.p.$description: Both facing sidebearings combined — one inter-letter gap (2× single); basis for word-spacing, in em.

typography.metric.default.cap-balance.$description: Bottom padding to vertically balance a filled single-line cell (e.g. inline code), in em.

typography.measure.tight.$description: Tighter measure (line length, in em). A more constrained alternative to the default.

typography.measure.default.$description: Default measure (line length, in em). Use as the comfortable maximum width to keep line lengths readable.

typography.type-step.150.font-size.$description: Type-step 150 font size. Loose-leading variant of step 100.

typography.type-step.200.font-size.$description: Default type-step font size. Type-steps are size/leading pairs for explicit typographic control without a full text composite (body/heading).

typography.type-step.450.font-size.$description: Type-step 450 font size. Loose-leading variant of step 400.

effect.opacity.disabled.$description: Opacity for disabled controls. A fallback for when color treatments (e.g. muted foreground, subtle background) can't fully convey the state.

effect.opacity.demoted.$description: Opacity for de-emphasised content. Use for elements pushed visually into the background but still perceivable (e.g. dimming surrounding content to draw attention to a focused element).

effect.shadow.default.$description: Default elevation shadow. Use on any element that should appear lifted above the page (cards, popovers, controls).

effect.stroke.inset.$description: Inset stroke. Use with outset to create a decorative offset stroke effect (e.g. on cards). Applied at the block-end and inline-end edges.

effect.stroke.outset.$description: Outset stroke. Use with inset to create a decorative offset stroke effect (e.g. on cards). Applied at the block-start and inline-start edges.

effect.filter.image.$description: Image filter. Use on imagery (photos, illustrations) to apply a styled image treatment.

color.brand.primary.$description: Primary brand color. Use for prominent brand expressions.

color.brand.support.$description: Supporting brand color. A decorative accent (e.g. strokes, patterns). Not contrast-safe; don't use for text, icons, or interactive elements.

color.logo.default.$description: Logo color. Use as the fill for the brand mark.

color.logo.neutral.$description: Neutral logo color. Use when the branded logo color would clash with surrounding content (e.g. over imagery, in monochrome contexts).

color.background.default.$description: Default page background. Use for the main canvas behind content.

color.background.panel.$description: Elevated surface background. Use for cards, modals, and other contained surfaces that sit above the page.

color.background.subtle.$description: Low-contrast surface background. Use for small discrete surfaces (inline code, zebra stripes, disabled inputs) that need light differentiation.

color.background.scrim.$description: Translucent overlay. Use as a backdrop behind overlay surfaces (e.g. modals, drawers) to dim underlying content while keeping it partially visible.

color.foreground.default.$description: Default foreground color. Use as the system's standard color for text and icons.

color.foreground.prose.$description: Body copy color.  Slightly softer than the default foreground for visual comfort.

color.foreground.muted.text.$description: Muted text color. Use for secondary text (helper copy, metadata, disabled labels) where lower emphasis is appropriate.

color.foreground.muted.non-text.$description: Muted foreground for non-text shapes that should recede (e.g. inactive icons and control surfaces, slider tracks). Reduced contrast, but still perceivable.

color.foreground.contrast.$description: Contrast foreground. Use for text and icons placed over saturated colored fills (brand, interactive, status, avatar) where the default foreground would lack sufficient contrast.

color.border.default.$description: Default border color. Use for standard borders and dividers.

color.border.brand.$description: Brand-tinted border. A decorative brand flourish (e.g. interactive cards, code blocks).

color.border.subtle.$description: Low-contrast border. Use where the border should recede visually.

color.interactive.default.$description: Default interactive color. Use for links and primary actionable elements in their resting state.

color.interactive.visited.$description: Visited interactive color for links the user has already followed. Inherits the default interactive color.

color.interactive.hover.$description: Hover state color for interactive elements.

color.interactive.focus.$description: Focus indicator color. Use for focus rings and keyboard-focus outlines on any interactive element.

color.interactive.active.$description: Active (pressed) state color for interactive elements.

color.interactive.neutral.default.$description: Neutral interactive color. Use for links and actions that shouldn't compete with brand-colored interactive elements (control labels, secondary controls, navigation).

color.interactive.neutral.visited.$description: Visited state color for neutral interactive elements. Inherits the default neutral interactive color.

color.interactive.neutral.hover.$description: Hover state color for neutral interactive elements.

color.interactive.neutral.focus.$description: Focus state for neutral interactive elements. Inherits the standard interactive focus color for consistency across element types.

color.interactive.neutral.active.$description: Active (pressed) state color for neutral interactive elements.

color.interactive.prose.default.$description: Inline link color for prose. Pairs with `foreground.prose`. Tuned for sufficient contrast against the softer prose text color.

color.interactive.prose.hover.$description: Hover state color for prose links.

color.interactive.prose.hover-decoration.$description: Underline color for prose links on hover.

color.interactive.prose.focus.$description: Focus state color for prose links.

color.interactive.prose.active.$description: Active (pressed) state color for prose links.

color.interactive.prose.active-decoratio.$description: Underline color for prose links during active (pressed) state.

color.intent.info.default.$description: Informational status color. Use for foreground content (text, icons) and borders conveying information or neutral notices.

color.intent.info.subtle.$description: Subtle info background. Use as a fill behind info messages.

color.intent.live.default.$description: Live status color. Use for foreground content (text, icons) and borders conveying live or on-air state.

color.intent.live.subtle.$description: Subtle live background. Use as a fill behind live indicators.

color.intent.pending.default.$description: Pending status color. Use for foreground content (text, icons) and borders conveying in-progress or unresolved state.

color.intent.pending.subtle.$description: Subtle pending background. Use as a fill behind pending indicators.

color.intent.success.default.$description: Success status color. Use for foreground content (text, icons) and borders conveying positive outcomes.

color.intent.success.subtle.$description: Subtle success background. Use as a fill behind success messages.

color.intent.warning.default.$description: Warning status color. Use for foreground content (text, icons) and borders conveying caution.

color.intent.warning.subtle.$description: Subtle warning background. Use as a fill behind warning messages.

color.intent.danger.default.$description: Danger status color. Use for foreground content (text, icons) and borders conveying failure, destructive action, or high-salience attention.

color.intent.danger.subtle.$description: Subtle danger background. Use as a fill behind error messages and notification indicators.

color.base16.00.$description: Base16 palette slot 00. Default background for code blocks and syntax-highlighted regions.

color.base16.01.$description: Base16 palette slot 01. Lighter background variant (panels, gutters in code views).

color.base16.03.$description: Base16 palette slot 03. Comments, invisibles, and line highlights.

color.base16.04.$description: Base16 palette slot 04. Dark foreground for status bars and chrome around code blocks.

color.base16.05.$description: Base16 palette slot 05. Default foreground color for code text.

color.base16.06.$description: Base16 palette slot 06. Light foreground variant for emphasised tokens.

color.base16.07.$description: Base16 palette slot 07. Light background variant.

color.base16.08.$description: Base16 palette slot 08. Variables, errors, and deletions.

color.base16.09.$description: Base16 palette slot 09. Integers, booleans, constants, and numeric literals.

color.base16.0a.$description: Base16 palette slot 0a. Classes, search highlight backgrounds.

color.base16.0b.$description: Base16 palette slot 0b. Strings, additions, and inherited colors.

color.base16.0c.$description: Base16 palette slot 0c. Regular expressions and escape characters.

color.base16.0d.$description: Base16 palette slot 0d. Functions, methods, and headings.

color.base16.0e.$description: Base16 palette slot 0e. Keywords, storage, and language directives.

color.base16.0f.$description: Base16 palette slot 0f. Deprecated, opening/closing tags, and embedded language markers.

color.avatar.default.$description: Default avatar background. Use as a fallback when no palette slot has been assigned. Slots 01–09 provide a palette for distinguishable per-user backgrounds when no uploaded image is available.
